title: Trace gateway: per-tenant routing, local buffering, and mTLS export
creator: Ariana Velasquez
description: Build a lightweight Trace Gateway service that accepts OpenTelemetry (OTLP) spans from Redwood agents/sidecars and performs per-tenant routing to downstream tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, or customer-managed endpoints). The gateway must provide: 1) per-tenant dynamic routing rules, 2) local fast persistent buffering for short-term backend outages, 3) batched export with backpressure-aware retries and exponential backoff, and 4) mutual TLS (mTLS) support for exporting to customer-managed backends. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, CI, and gradual rollout with feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gateway accepts OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP traces and applies tenant routing rules defined in runtime config. 2) When downstream is unavailable, gateway persists up to 10GB of traces locally and drains them when healthy. 3) Exports are performed batched (configurable batch size and interval), with idempotent retry semantics and jittered exponential backoff. 4) mTLS can be configured per-destination via KMS-backed certs and rotates without gateway restart. 5) Integration test exercising Tempo and Jaeger exporters passes in CI. 6) Feature gated rollout to 10% of internal traffic, with metrics and SLO dashboards available.
design_decisions:
- Use a small Go service (trace-gateway) colocated in the control plane fleet to minimize network hops.
- Routing rules stored in central config (etcd) and pushed via streaming watch; fallback to local config on control-plane partition.
- Local buffering implemented with a circular write-ahead log on SSD + small in-memory queue for hot paths. This gives bounded disk usage and crash recovery.
- Exporter workers are per-destination with token bucket rate limiting; retries are coordinated via a per-export checkpoint to avoid duplicate bursts.
- mTLS handled via a pluggable vault/KMS adapter; cert reload via SIGHUP or admin API.
- Chosen to translate/normalize OTLP attributes into our standard tenant/route headers to support legacy Jaeger backends that expect certain tags.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit tests + end-to-end local tests (2 weeks). Phase 2: Internal dogfood in staging with synthetic traffic, enable on internal tenant only (1 week). Phase 3: Gradual canary: 1%, 5%, 10% of production traces for non-critical customers (3 weeks) behind feature flag. Phase 4: Enable for all tenants with opt-in for mTLS destinations (monitor for error spike). Abort criteria: sustained export error rate > 2% for 24h or disk buffer fill > 80% capacity.
telemetry_and_alerts: New metrics: gateway.received_spans, gateway.exported_spans, gateway.export_errors, gateway.buffer_fill_bytes, gateway.buffer_drain_rate, gateway.mtls_handshakes_failed. Alert rules: P1 if export_errors > 1% sustained for 10m for any production tenant; P0 if buffer_fill_bytes > 90% of configured capacity. Dashboards: per-tenant export latency heatmap, downstream availability chart, buffer occupancy over time. Traces: end-to-end trace flow includes gateway span with route decision and export outcome tags.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for routing logic and config watch.
- Integration tests: OTLP->gateway->tempo and OTLP->gateway->jaeger in CI using ephemeral dockerized backends.
- Chaos test injecting backend failures and verifying buffer durability and drain.
- Load test to validate batching/backpressure behavior (QPS targets 10k spans/s per instance).
- Security test for mTLS handshake and cert rotation flow.
- Compliance review to ensure no tenant data leaks across routes.
